sections.skill: Recognize signs of identity theft and follow the steps to recover

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa gets a bill for a credit card she never opened. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: The bank sends random cards to everyone as a gift
Her credit score rose and a card opened by itself
It is a normal reminder to apply for a card
Someone used her identity

questions.intro: Identity theft is when someone uses your personal information, such as your name and Social Security number, to open accounts, file taxes, or get services. Signs include unfamiliar bills, accounts on your credit report, or calls from debt collectors about debts you do not owe.
questions.feedback: An unknown account is a key sign of identity theft.

misconceptions.A: Banks do not open accounts without applications
misconceptions.C: Misreads a bill as an offer

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa learns that someone opened a credit card account in her name. Which step should she take early to help prevent more new-credit fraud?

choices.text: Freeze her credit at all three bureaus
Post her Social Security number to warn friends
Wait a year to see if it happens again
Close her own savings account and keep cash at home

questions.correct_answer: Freeze her credit at all three bureaus
questions.intro: A credit freeze limits access to your credit report, so most lenders that check it cannot approve new credit in your name until you lift the freeze. It is free at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. It does not stop misuse of existing accounts or every kind of identity theft, so also contact the business where the fraud happened and review your reports.
questions.feedback: Freezing all three reports helps block new credit accounts; it does not protect existing accounts.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: The IRS rejects Rosa's e-filed return because a return was already filed with her SSN. What may this indicate, and what should she do?

choices.text: She filed twice by accident, so she should ignore it
Her employer filed her return for her
Possible tax identity theft; investigate with the IRS
The IRS lost her return, so nothing can be done

questions.correct_answer: Possible tax identity theft; investigate with the IRS
questions.intro: In tax identity theft, a thief files a return with someone else's SSN to steal a refund. A rejection for a duplicate SSN can also come from a filing or data error, such as a dependent claimed on another return, so check before concluding. The IRS offers an Identity Protection PIN to help prevent it.
questions.feedback: A duplicate-SSN rejection may signal tax identity theft; she should check for errors and follow the IRS identity theft steps.

misconceptions.B: Employers do not file personal returns
